season_context.local_season_notes: Climate ranges from harsh northern winters, where down outerwear is essential, to milder southern cities. November's Singles' Day sales open peak season, followed by year-end and Spring Festival (Lunar New Year, early 2027) buying of red, festive and new-Chinese-style clothing. Shanghai Fashion Week SS27 ran in October.

trends.name: New Chinese style goes mainstream and global
trends.summary: Xin zhongshi blends Chinese elements with modern design using easier fabrics and looser cuts, such as relaxed qipao shapes; after a viral clip, Western houses including Ralph Lauren, Kenzo and Lemaire echoed it for fall 2026.

trends.name: Frog-button track tops
trends.summary: Adidas Originals' Lunar New Year track jacket, with mandarin collar and frog fastenings at around 1,000 yuan, sold out across China before Spring Festival and spawned resale premiums and lookalikes abroad.

trends.name: Horse-face skirt demand surge
trends.summary: Orders for the pleated mamianqun in Caoxian, China's hanfu hub, reportedly ran about ten times higher in early 2026 than a year earlier, with makers blending in international styling and exporting to dozens of countries.

trends.name: Lighter heritage brocades
trends.summary: Producers are modernising traditional brocades: Yun brocade patterns on horse-face skirts and Zhuang brocade woven on jacquard lines to cut weight, feeding a new-Chinese-style market said to exceed 100 billion yuan.

trends.name: Metallic embroidery and cross-stitch zodiac motifs
trends.summary: For Lunar New Year 2026, Burberry redrew its Knight emblem as an ink-and-watercolour horse rendered in metallic embroidery, cross-stitch and appliqued badges, anchored by an exclusive red check.

trends.name: Zodiac jacquard and red knitwear capsules
trends.summary: Thom Browne's Year of the Horse range used horse embroidery, jacquard and leatherwork, intarsia cardigans and red knits, showing how luxury houses localise festive drops for Chinese shoppers.

trends.name: Cautious recovery, local brands and resale
trends.summary: Bain expects China's personal luxury market to edge back to modest growth in 2026 after two years of decline, with domestic brands gaining share and secondhand luxury expanding 15-20 percent in 2025.

trends.name: Artisanal upcycling on the Shanghai runway
trends.summary: Maison Margiela's first show outside Paris closed Shanghai AW26, mixing ready-to-wear with couture built from porcelain, beeswax and upcycled vintage pieces.

trends.name: Down jackets as fashion statements
trends.summary: Bosideng's 50th-anniversary Paris debut presented down as sculptural eveningwear and city tailoring, mixing Song brocade, Shanghai qipao-style cutting and Art Deco lines and ending with pink down evening looks.

trends.name: Coquettish bows and faux fur
trends.summary: Shanghai AW26 leaned on girlish bows, nostalgic colour pairings and faux fur, often fusing them as fur stoles knotted into oversized bows on 1930s-inspired silhouettes at labels such as Shushu/Tong.

trends.name: Animal prints and bubble skirts
trends.summary: Jacques Wei paired leopard and other animal-print outerwear with bubble skirts, colourful tights and leather for AW26, while Xu Zhi moved from military coats to leopard and iridescent satins.

trends.name: Premium natural fibres and elastane-free stretch
trends.summary: Intertextile Shanghai's August fair spotlighted organic cotton, linen, Lenzing fibres, silk and cashmere, plus wool-cashmere-mohair stretch cloth made without elastane that resists creasing.

trends.name: Low-impact dyeing and finishing
trends.summary: Denim mills at Intertextile Shanghai showed waterless finishing and lower-impact indigo dyeing, while surface-design and embroidery exhibitors mixed technical innovation with handwork and handloomed heritage cloth.

trends.name: Climate-adaptive and pet textiles
trends.summary: Intertextile's 2026 autumn edition added a pet-apparel fabric zone and a lab for fabrics that regulate temperature and humidity, signalling new demand from pet fashion and hotter, more variable climates.

trends.name: Premium activewear as new luxury
trends.summary: Chinese shoppers kept trading up in sports and outdoor gear, treating premium activewear as health-linked luxury; running and hiking lead activities and outdoor events for children have multiplied over the past decade.

trends.name: Gorpcore as a fashion cycle
trends.summary: Context from late 2025: much technical outdoor gear in China is bought for status and style rather than performance, with rental and resale growing and analysts expecting a split between image-led and specialist brands.

trends.name: Samoyed white
trends.summary: Pantone's white colour of the year was renamed Samoyed white on Xiaohongshu, with young consumers linking white clothing to calm, healing and emotional-luxury moods.

trends.name: Autumn palette from China Fashion Week
trends.summary: Earlier season context: Pantone's Beijing AW25/26 report featured calming greens, blue-greys, red ochre, creamy beige, soft pink and roast brown as key runway shades.

trends.name: Guochao 3.0: heritage and regional craft
trends.summary: Jing Daily lists a third wave of national-trend consumption centred on intangible cultural heritage and regional identity, alongside a 'less but better' shift toward fewer, higher-quality purchases.

trends.name: Bespoke qipao and heritage tailoring
trends.summary: Shanghai's couture and tailoring festival pushed made-to-measure qipao, suits and new-Chinese-style wear, with kesi weaving, blue calico and hand embroidery demonstrations and AI-based remote measuring.

trends.name: Domestic designer labels lead Gen Z wardrobes
trends.summary: Chinese Gen Z increasingly favours home-grown, digitally savvy labels such as Shushu/Tong, Yvmin, Ming Ma and Rocksteady over imported brands.

trends.name: Nineties Hong Kong noir tailoring
trends.summary: Shao's SS27 drew on 1990s Hong Kong gangster films: open chalk-stripe waistcoats, sharp shoulders, high-slit satin skirts and draped puff-sleeve menswear clipped with metal fasteners.

trends.name: Reworked qipao and Tang jackets
trends.summary: Ao Yes updated qipao and Tang-dynasty jackets for SS27 with stand collars, tiered ruffles, sequins, rippling water-like stripes, sunlight polka dots and Song-court textile references.

trends.name: Lace softness against armoured shoulders
trends.summary: Yirantian contrasted sheer lace tops, asymmetric skirts and capes with rigid corsets and padded, armour-like jackets with exaggerated shoulders and chests for SS27.

trends.name: Lingerie sheers and lace
trends.summary: Xu Zhi's SS27 used sheer slips, ruffled chemises, lace-edged bloomers and crinoline pinafores, with thread-built corset tops and skirts that split into ribbons, including menswear.

trends.name: Office-uniform subversion
trends.summary: Staffonly played with corporate dress for SS27: off-centre plackets, ties worn backwards or knotted into bows, jackets fastened with stationery clips, schoolboy shorts and wire-shaped hoodies.

trends.name: Intense colour blocking with satin and lace
trends.summary: Shushu/Tong's SS27 paired intense colour blocks with flower-shaped puff skirts, petal edges, handmade lace, coloured satin and schoolgirl dresses and sets.

trends.name: Naive and blurred florals
trends.summary: Shushu/Tong scattered childlike buds on knits, daisies on a sheer mini and a softly blurred floral across a knee-length coat in its SS27 collection.

trends.name: Virtual and AI-generated fashion
trends.summary: Beijing's SS27 fashion week included immersive showcases by more than ten virtual designers, 3D and AIGC artists, plus support schemes for young designers working with intangible heritage.
